report:
Finding: Model B is biased toward culinary/food/recipe/restaurant content (vs. Model A).

Reasoning:
- Logit-lens tokens at the highest-norm cells are overwhelmingly food/culinary/restaurant terms across layers and positions: “Cooking/cooking,” “Restaurant/restaurant,” “Chef,” “Kitchen,” “baking/Baked/Baker,” “Cake/Cheesecake,” “microwave,” “Professional/professional,” “Cook,” “kitchen,” “cooked,” “restaurant(s).” This pattern becomes very consistent from roughly L16 onward and persists through L25 across p1–p4 (and even shows at p0 in later layers).
- Related lifestyle/blog signals also appear: “blogs/blogging/blogger,” “hottest [restaurants],” and marketing-ish tokens (“ad,” “Magazine,” “Creative,” “Market,” “Mail”), consistent with food-blog/culinary editorial style.
- The difference norm is concentrated in later layers (L18–L25), suggesting a shift in higher-level semantics/style rather than low-level tokenization effects. It affects multiple early token positions, indicating a general generation bias rather than a single-token artifact.

Conclusion: The evidence supports a domain/style shift where Model B is more inclined toward culinary/recipe/restaurant (food blog/professional kitchen) vocabulary and themes.
